newsitem.title: FRANCE: Euro-court takes British boy's anti-spanking case.
newsitem.headline: Euro-court takes British boy's anti-spanking case.

text.p: The European Commission of Human Rights said on Monday it had agreed to take up the case of a 12-year-old British boy who is challenging the right of his parents to smack him.
The decision is the first step on the way to a possible ruling by the European Court of Human Rights, on the legality of corporal punishment in British homes.

The boy, who lives with his natural father but cannot be named for legal reasons, based his case on an incident three years ago when he was beaten with a cane by his stepfather after trying to stab another child with a kitchen knife. His stepfather was taken to court on charges of assault but was acquitted.

Lawyers acting for the boy are expected to argue that the British government failed to protect the child's human rights. His natural father is backing him in the case but his mother has defended her right to punish her son, saying he had been "totally out of control" since a toddler.

Caning and other forms of corporal punishment were outlawed in British schools some years ago but courts have frequently acquitted parents who have admitted using canes, belts and electric flexes to beat their children at home.
Britain's conservative government has criticised the rights court in a series of recent rulings that it says constitute outside meddling in its ability to govern.
